disclaimer.title: Everstead is not a legal service.
disclaimer.body: Plans cover organisation, storage, access for the people you choose and reminders. They do not include will drafting, legal advice or any regulated professional service. Everstead is built to sit alongside your solicitor and adviser, not to replace them.

faq.title: Everything you might want to know.

items.q: How does the free plan work?
items.a: It needs no card and it never expires. You get 5 accounts, 5 documents and 3 trusted people, with 1 GB of storage, and everything else is open: Your AI Assistant, About Me, instructions and final wishes, the apps and the export. It is a plan, not a trial.

items.q: How does the Everstead+ trial work?
items.a: Everstead+ starts with 14 days free. A card is needed to begin, nothing is charged until the 14 days end, and if you cancel before then you pay nothing. During the trial you have the whole plan.

items.q: What happens when I cancel Everstead+?
items.a: You keep Everstead+ until the end of the period you have paid for. Then your vault moves to the free plan: nothing is deleted, everything you added stays, and the free plan's limits apply only to new additions. You can export a complete copy of your vault, files included, at any time from Settings.

One subscription covers two people, each with a vault of their own. A couple can each organise their own affairs, see only what the other chooses to share, and never have to pour two lives into one account.

items.q: Is there a discount for yearly billing?
items.a: Yes. Billed yearly, Everstead+ costs {{perYear}} a year instead of {{monthlyTotal}}, which saves {{saving}}. The yearly rate applies from the first day and stays the same for the year.

Yes, at any time from Settings. An upgrade takes effect immediately. A downgrade takes effect at the end of the period you have already paid for, and you are never charged for more than the plan you are on.
Yes, for iPhone and Android, on the same plan as the web. In the iPhone app you can also subscribe through the App Store, which shows its own price and handles its own cancellation.

No. Everstead is an organisation and planning tool. It does not draft wills, give legal advice or provide any regulated professional service. It is designed to sit alongside your solicitor, financial adviser and other professionals. For the legal side of your estate, use a qualified solicitor.

All data is encrypted in transit and at rest with AES-256. Everstead operates under UK GDPR and is registered with the ICO. Everstead staff cannot read the content of your plan, and access to it is controlled entirely by you.

items.q: What about firms, employers and care providers?
items.a: They buy something different: the ability to send documents into people's own vaults and ask for one item at a time, without holding any of it. That is Everstead for Business, priced by the size of the organisation and sold on a call.

items.q: Is it worth it if I only set it up once?
items.a: Setting it up once is already the point: the people you love will not spend months piecing your life together if something happens. But most of what you add changes over time. Accounts open and close, people move, a document gets replaced. Everstead is where those changes go, so the plan stays true, and on the free plan that costs nothing.
